analysis.subject: computing
analysis.pageCoverage: Page covers definition of AI and NSF-supported research areas including computer vision and ImageNet, stochastic modeling, neural networks and protein prediction, reinforcement learning, and intelligent tutoring illustrated by Duolingo.

overview.headline: How decades of AI research built tools for vision, prediction and learning

keyPoints.point: Students explain that AI is technology enabling computer systems to learn and reason to make decisions.
keyPoints.quote: AI is a technology that enables computer systems to learn, reason and make decisions

keyPoints.point: Students describe how techniques perfected on the ImageNet database became central to everyday recognition technologies.
keyPoints.quote: Techniques perfected on this database became central to technologies like Face ID, tagging friends in photos and detecting tumors in MRI scans.

keyPoints.point: Students explain stochastic modeling as capturing real-world randomness to improve navigation and communication systems.
keyPoints.quote: stochastic modeling is the idea of capturing real-world randomness mathematically.

keyPoints.point: Students trace how reinforcement learning advances through trial and error and reward-based decision optimization.
keyPoints.quote: Reinforcement learning is a type of machine learning where an AI system learns from trial and error

keyTerms.gloss: Systems that interpret pixels as meaningful patterns to recognize objects and faces.
keyTerms.quote: Computer vision emerged in the early 1960s as researchers began exploring whether machines could learn to see and interpret simple patterns and objects.

keyTerms.gloss: Publicly available image collection used to train and test vision models for comparison.
keyTerms.quote: and her team launched ImageNet, a publicly available database containing more than 3 million images

keyTerms.gloss: Mathematical approach for capturing randomness to model unpredictable natural and technical processes.
keyTerms.quote: stochastic modeling is the idea of capturing real-world randomness mathematically.

keyTerms.gloss: Computational models inspired by the brain that power photo generation and drug design applications.
keyTerms.quote: Neural networks — computational models inspired by the human brain — power technologies like photo-generation apps, digital assistants and advanced drug design.

keyTerms.gloss: Machine learning approach where a system learns from trial and error using rewards for actions.
keyTerms.quote: Reinforcement learning is a type of machine learning where an AI system learns from trial and error

keyTerms.gloss: AI-driven tutoring that bridges student ability and expert problem solving with personalized actions.
keyTerms.quote: intelligent tutoring systems, which aim to bridge the gap between students' current ability and expert-level problem-solving

componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: Helps students link each research area to concrete everyday examples the page provides for comparison.
componentPlan.focusQuote: Researchers use large, high-quality image datasets to train and test deep learning systems, helping them compare and improve computer vision models.

componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: Builds chronological reasoning by ordering breakthroughs from early vision work to modern language learning apps.
componentPlan.focusQuote: Computer vision emerged in the early 1960s as researchers began exploring whether machines could learn to see and interpret simple patterns and objects.
